title: 369. Palindrome Permutation II

examples.explanation: Halves "ab" and "ba" mirror to full palindromes "abba" and "baab".
Three different characters mean more than one odd count, so no palindrome exists.
All characters match, giving a single distinct palindrome.

hints: Count characters first; more than one odd count means the answer is empty.
Build palindromes from half the characters plus the middle character, permuting only the half uniquely.
